name: Three-way meeting
detail: Ministry of Finance, Bank of Japan and the FSA met after a 34-year low — a deliberate, visible signal of readiness.

name: Intervention · record day
detail: ¥5.92tn (≈$40.8bn) of dollars sold — a single-day record at the time, executed during Golden Week when liquidity is thin. Spot 160.245.

name: Intervention · second leg
detail: A further ¥3.87tn (≈$26bn). Period total ¥9.79tn, roughly $67bn.

name: Kanda: on high alert
detail: Currency chief Kanda: authorities “seriously concerned and on high alert” near a 38-year low. Intervention followed 15 days later.

name: Intervention · into a US miss
detail: ¥5.53tn (≈$36.8bn), spot 161.76 → 157.30. Fired on a day the dollar was already offered on a weak US CPI print — pushing with the tide.

name: The unwind
detail: Carry positions closed en masse. Spot −7.6% in one week, the largest weekly move in this dataset. Nasdaq 100 sold off hard; VIX printed its third-largest spike on record.

name: BOJ to 0.50%
detail: First step of a genuine tightening cycle rather than an experiment. Passed 8–1.

name: Fed begins cutting
detail: First of three consecutive quarter-point cuts, taking the US rate toward 3.50–3.75% by December. The gap starts closing from the American side.

name: Japan–US currency understanding
detail: A cooperation understanding between Tokyo and Washington, later referenced by Mimura as working in cooperation since September. Date approximate.

name: Fed cuts again
detail: Second consecutive quarter-point reduction.

name: Fed to 3.50–3.75%
detail: Third and final cut of the cycle. Held at this level throughout 2026 to date.

name: BOJ to 0.75%
detail: Unanimous. Takata and Tamura dissented only on the price-outlook wording, not the rate.

name: First warnings of the cycle
detail: Mimura on “appropriate” action against excessive moves; Katayama on speculative moves and import costs.

name: BOJ holds; yen +1.7%
detail: A hold from near an 18-month low. Note the pattern — Japanese intervention repeatedly clusters around hold decisions, when the disappointment sells the currency off.

name: Rate checks · Tokyo and Washington
detail: Officials called banks for live prices in both capitals. Spot moved roughly 159 → 152. Ministry data released 30 January confirmed zero yen was spent.

name: Mimura’s first “decisive”
detail: Described as the strongest warning to that point, and the first use of the word. No intervention followed for a month.

name: BOJ holds at 0.75%, 6–3
detail: Three of nine favoured an increase. Two days later, intervention.

name: “Final advisory” · intervention same day
detail: Katayama said the time for bold steps was nearing; Mimura gave his “final advisory.” ¥6,278.7bn (≈$39bn) deployed that session. Spot 160.72 → 155.5.

name: Intervention · follow-through
detail: ¥780.2bn, a small continuation.

name: Intervention · third leg
detail: ¥4,675.9bn. Period total ¥11,734.9bn, about $72.5bn — a record month at the time.

name: BOJ to 1.00%
detail: Highest Japanese policy rate since 1995. Passed 7–1 with Asada dissenting; Ueda absent, Himino chairing.

name: 40-year low
detail: Spot reached 163.99 — the weakest the yen had been against the dollar in four decades.

name: Fed holds, 9–3
detail: Three dissents — Hammack, Kashkari, Logan — all in favour of raising. Unusual, and the start of market pricing for a US hike.

name: Intervention · largest on record
detail: Venue volumes roughly nine times normal. Spot 164.0 → 157.8. Period total ¥15,399.3bn, about $97bn.

name: The United States joins
detail: First US operation in the yen market since 2011, buying yen with euros rather than dollars. South Korea acted alongside. Estimates of the US leg run $1–10bn — small, and explicitly a signal.

name: Warsh at Jackson Hole
detail: The Fed chair: the committee must be confident inflation is moving to target “clearly and at sufficient speed — otherwise, we have work to do.” Hike odds rose to roughly two thirds.

name: Takata on the pace
detail: A board member’s remarks on the size of future increases moved spot 160.39 → around 158 in US hours — a Tokyo-hours utterance worth more than two yen.

name: Bessent meets Katayama and Ueda
detail: The US Treasury Secretary met Japan’s finance minister and central bank governor at the G20, saying he was confident Japan would act in ways leading to a stronger yen. Spot fell toward 155.50.
